subject: Request: Availability & Regional Latency Carveouts — Order Form Language and MSA Attachment
messages:
From: Alison Park <alison.park@clearviewhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-16T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA carveouts for order form / MSA attachment

Naomi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our infra team reviewed the MSA and have two outstanding asks before we can route to legal: a) a clear carveout for regional latency credits tied to multi-region failover windows, and b) optional language on order form that enumerates an availability bucket for batch inference (we run scheduled large-batch jobs overnight).

We attached a redlined MSA (see ClearView_MSA_Draft_v3.pdf) and a short spreadsheet with observed latency targets (latency-evidence-playbook.xlsx). Can Redwood propose concise order-form phrasing and a one-paragraph addendum for the MSA that defines when credits apply vs operational maintenance? We want minimal custom text in the SOW but explicit triggers in the order form.

If you have a recommended playbook for evidence (metrics/trace windows) to validate a claim for a credit, please include it — our ops team needs to know what telemetry you require.

Appreciate a quick path — procurement is hoping to finish sign-off by end of next week.

Best,
Alison Park
Head of Procurement
ClearView Health

Attachments: ClearView_MSA_Draft_v3.pdf (PDF, redlines); latency-evidence-playbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alison Park <alison.park@clearviewhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-16T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA carveouts for order form / MSA attachment

Hi Alison —

Thanks for the redlines and the latency spreadsheet — that's super helpful. I can absolutely draft two things for you: (1) concise order-form language that enumerates availability buckets (interactive vs batch) and explicit credit triggers for regional failover/latency breaches, and (2) a short MSA addendum paragraph that references the order form for detailed thresholds so the MSA stays high-level.

Before I draft, two quick clarifying Qs from our side so we align on scope:
- For batch inference windows, do you expect strict per-job SLAs (e.g., 95% of batch jobs complete within X hours) or is this an availability-tier statement ("batch availability subject to scheduled window, credits only for failed scheduled runs")?
- On evidence: is the ClearView ops team comfortable sharing a sample trace (span id + request id) for one window to validate telemetry alignment, or do you prefer Redwood provide a telemetry spec and you produce the payloads?

I'll loop in Karthik for the order-form language (cost/credit math) and Ben for the telemetry/evidence playbook. We can aim to send you a redline and a short execution note today.

Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-16T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA carveouts for order form / MSA attachment

Team —

Draft notes below for Naomi to include in the reply to ClearView. Kept the language intentionally short so procurement/legal can drop into the order form and the MSA references it.

Proposed order-form snippets (keep as bullets for the form UI):
- "Service Availability (interactive): 99.9% monthly uptime per region; credits apply when sustained region-level 5xx error rate >2% for 30m or rolling 15m p95 latency exceeds 1.5x committed threshold."
- "Batch Inference Window (scheduled jobs): Jobs scheduled during the agreed window are covered under 'Batch Availability'. A credit is only triggered when >25% of scheduled jobs fail to start or complete within the scheduled window without prior notice. Credits capped at 25% of monthly usage attributed to batch jobs."
- "Regional Failover: If traffic is routed to an adjacent region due to Redwood-initiated region-level outage, a reduced credit applies (10% of monthly affected usage); full credits require documented sustained regional outage >4 hours despite Redwood's failover attempts."

Evidence & telemetry: Redwood will accept tracing artifacts or aggregated request logs containing: timestamp, request_id, route_id, region, status_code, service_latency_ms. For privacy, ClearView may sanitize PII. Accepted formats: newline-delimited JSON or CSV with headers.

Cost/credit note: For non-standard credit calculations (batch-heavy accounts), we recommend a capped credit schedule in the order form with explicit attribution of monthly usage to batch vs interactive tokens. We can provide a short table with examples for the order form UI.

Kimberly, can you flag anything in the MSA addendum that would be problematic if phrased as: "Availability thresholds and credit triggers are defined in the applicable order form and shall govern the Service Commitment for that Order"?

Karthik
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alison Park <alison.park@clearviewhealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@clearviewhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-16T15:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA carveouts for order form / MSA attachment

Alison —

Thanks for the quick turn. Based on your spreadsheet and our follow-up, attached are two things: 1) "OrderForm_SLA_Snippets.txt" (below) with copy you can paste into the order form UI, and 2) a one-paragraph MSA addendum we propose to keep the MSA high-level while pointing to the order form for details. I also included a short evidence spec so your ops team knows the minimal telemetry we need.

Order form language (suggested paste):
- Service Availability (Interactive): 99.9% monthly uptime per region. Credits apply when sustained region-level error rate exceeds 2% for 30 minutes or when rolling 15-minute p95 latency exceeds 1.5x the committed threshold in the applicable order form.
- Batch Inference Window (Scheduled Jobs): "Batch Availability" applies to jobs scheduled in the agreed window. Credits are triggered when more than 25% of scheduled jobs fail to start or complete within the scheduled window without prior written notice. Credits for batch failures are capped at 25% of the monthly usage attributed to batch jobs.
- Regional Failover Credit: If Redwood routes traffic to a secondary region due to a region-level degradation, a partial credit (10%) applies for impacted usage; full credits require a documented sustained regional outage exceeding four (4) continuous hours despite Redwood's documented remediation and failover attempts.

MSA addendum paragraph (proposed):
"Service Commitments and Credit Triggers: The parties agree that specific availability thresholds, latency commitments and credit calculations applicable to a given Order are defined in the applicable Order Form. The Order Form shall control with respect to the measurement windows, telemetry requirements, and credit allocation methodology for that Order. Except as otherwise provided in the Order Form, Redwood's standard measurement and mitigation procedures shall apply."

Telemetry spec (minimal): timestamp, request_id, route_id, region, status_code, latency_ms (p50/p95). Formats: NDJSON or CSV with headers. Minimum retention window for evidence: 30 days from incident.

Next steps: if this looks good, confirm and we'll prepare a tiny illustrative credit table for the order form (three scenarios) and route the MSA addendum to Kimberly for final legal sign-off. We can also include the DocuSign envelope link for the order form once legal signs.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: OrderForm_SLA_Snippets.txt (text), evidence-spec.md (text)
